new.title: Search for a Dispersion Measure Excess Toward Nearby Galaxy Halos Using Fast Radio Bursts from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog
new.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe foreground ionized baryons via their dispersion measures (DM). Using 1748 sub-arcminute-localized sources from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog, we conduct a statistical stacking study of the circumgalactic media (CGM) of nearby galaxies by analyzing the DMs of FRBs whose sightlines intersect foreground halos. For galaxy halos within 50 Mpc, we measure a mean DM excess of $119\pm44$ pc~cm$^{-3}$ $(p = 0.0053; \sim 2.6\sigma)$ within one virial radius. Expanding to 150 Mpc (628 intersections), we find a tentative decline in the mean DM as a function of impact parameter $(p = 0.0046; \sim 2.6\sigma)$, which is predominantly driven by typical Milky Way (MW)-like galaxies $(10 \leq \log(M_*/M_\odot)\leq 11)$. We use this DM profile to constrain parameters of the CGM electron density distribution, $n_e^\mathrm{CGM}(r) \propto r^{-3\beta}$, finding an extrapolated central electron density in the range of $(1.7-21.1) \times 10^{-3}\mathrm{\,cm}^{-3}$, with a radial power-law index of $\beta = 0.68^{+0.15}_{-0.16}$, consistent with constraints from X-ray stacking studies of MW-like galaxies. At very low impact parameters, we detect a significant DM deficit likely due to cross-matching FRBs that originate from galaxies within our galaxy sample. By deriving the DM-galaxy cross-correlation function, we show that this deficit matches theoretical predictions if 20 FRBs originate from galaxies within 150 Mpc, indicating that CHIME/FRB detects a higher fraction of low-$z$ FRBs than previously thought. We forecast that $10^4$ FRBs with similar localization errors will provide a 5-$\sigma$ detection of the CGM, and that FRBs at intermediate redshifts ($0.4\lesssim z_\mathrm{FRB}\lesssim 0.75$) are ideal for studying intervening CGMs.

new.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Black Holes: Non-Gaussianity and Accretion Evade $μ$-Distortion Constraints
new.summary: Recent JWST observations of "Little Red Dots" (LRDs) at $z \gtrsim 4$ suggest the existence of early supermassive black holes (SMBHs) with masses $\gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$. Their rapid emergence challenges conventional seeding and growth scenarios based on accretion and mergers of Population III stellar remnants, motivating renewed interest in primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from primordial perturbations. Explaining such massive seeds requires power spectrum enhancements that are constrained by cosmic microwave background (CMB) spectral distortions. In this work we perform the first comprehensive Bayesian exploration of non-Gaussian primordial perturbations capable of producing SMBH seeds while remaining consistent with CMB spectral distortion constraints, and examine the role of accretion history in constraining these models. We perform a suite of Markov chain Monte Carlo analyses of power spectrum enhancements (lognormal and cut-power-law) with varying local non-Gaussianity and accretion histories, satisfying the COBE/FIRAS $\mu$-distortion constraint with and without the requirement that the model produces SMBH seeds. We find that both models can seed LRDs and evade $\mu$-distortion bounds for $|f_{\rm NL}|= O(1)$ and peak amplitude $A= O(10^{-3})$, when standard Eddington-limited accretion is also incorporated. Interestingly, the results exhibit a preference for both positive and negative values of $f_{\rm NL}$. The preference for negative $f_{\rm NL}$ is strongly dependent on the accretion history, and is removed if the black holes have a small duty cycle, $f_{\rm duty}\lesssim 0.1$. These results demonstrate that the JWST high-$z$ LRD population can be seeded by primordial perturbations while remaining compatible with CMB data, and highlight the importance of next-generation CMB spectral distortion missions to test this hypothesis.

new.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars
new.summary: Brown dwarfs are rare as close companions to stars compared to planets and stellar companions, a paucity known as the brown dwarf desert. Whether the desert sits at a fixed companion mass or a fixed companion-to-star mass-ratio $q$ has been difficult to test, because microlensing, radial velocities, and direct imaging have sampled comparatively narrow slices of stellar mass and separation. Here we apply a novel joint-modelling method to Hipparcos and Gaia DR2/DR3 astrometry from 63,254 stars to complete this picture with a sample 1-2 orders of magnitude larger than those of previous wide-orbit demographic studies. For the first time, we present a single survey that measures occurrence rates of both planetary and stellar companions on 3--94 yr orbits ($\sim$2--20\,au) across host masses from M dwarfs to B stars. We find that the desert is a mass-ratio feature: companions are strongly depleted at $q\approx2\%$ independent of stellar mass from M to B stars, and a desert at fixed companion mass is excluded. Furthermore, we find a positive trend in occurrence with metallicity below the mass-ratio desert, but a negative trend above. The desert therefore separates two distinct populations, plausibly two formation channels, that each scale with stellar mass: the lightest stellar-like companions of K stars ($\sim13 \, M_{jup}$) are less massive than the heaviest planet-like companions of B stars ($\sim27, M_{jup}$), which continue well beyond the deuterium-burning limit. Mass-ratio, not mass, is therefore the physically meaningful boundary between planets and their stellar-like counterparts.

cross.title: Cosmic Corpses: Dead stars as Factories of the most Extreme Objects in the Universe
cross.summary: The apparent serenity of the night sky conceals a long history of stellar evolution, in which gravity and the properties of matter determine the remarkable fates of stars. In this pedagogical account, we discuss white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes, explaining how quantum mechanics, nuclear interactions, and General Relativity govern their formation and distinctive properties. We also highlight the possibility of primordial black holes, which may have formed from rare large density fluctuations in the early Universe, and briefly discuss their potential role as constituents of dark matter.

cross.title: Magnetohydrodynamic spectra and line invariants in the presence of axions
cross.summary: A new form of the mean-field equations for magnetic fields, which accounts for the interaction with axions, is studied. It is shown that the asymptotic ergodic invariants of magnetic field lines play a key role in the evolution of magnetic fields, which determine the type of the magnetohydrodynamic spectrum of the solutions.

cross.title: Collider-observable curvaton
cross.summary: We study a technically natural realization of the curvaton mechanism, in which decay is mediated through the superrenormalizable interaction with the Higgs. We compute the quantum and thermal corrections to the curvaton potential and show that they remain under control throughout its cosmological evolution. For high inflationary scales, the curvaton dissipates through off-shell processes in the Standard Model plasma. The viable parameter space is broad, and the region in which the curvaton mass and dimensionful Higgs-portal coupling are closest in scale lies within the discovery reach of proposed searches for light Higgs-mixed scalars.

cross.title: Scalable early warning for binary neutron-star mergers in third-generation gravitational-wave detectors
cross.summary: Third-generation gravitational-wave observatories will observe binary neutron-star coalescences for hours before merger. Over these extended time windows, Earth's motion and the long signal durations make standard search methods computationally demanding for low-latency detection. We propose an approach based on short-time Fourier transforms and convolutional neural networks that implicitly marginalizes over extrinsic parameters, effectively reducing the search to the chirp mass. The network learns the signals' nonlinear time-frequency morphology, approximating the optimal Bayesian detection statistic. Using a large-scale campaign of simulated signal injections, we compare the network's performance with a GPU-optimized matched-filtering baseline for both the ET$\Delta$ and ET2L configurations of the Einstein Telescope and signal durations from approximately 25 minutes ($f_{\rm min} = 5$ Hz) to approximately 6 hours ($f_{\rm min} = 2$ Hz). The network achieves comparable detection sensitivity while reducing computational costs by over four orders of magnitude, bringing processing times from minutes to milliseconds. This efficiency paves the way for rapid early-warning alerts for multi-messenger astronomy in the third-generation detector era.

cross.title: Relativistic Simulations of Self-Gravitating Radiation Fluids
cross.summary: We present an approach for numerical simulations of pure radiation fluids within the general relativistic hydrodynamics framework. The approach models radiation as a self-gravitating perfect fluid with vanishing rest mass, enabling simulations of radiation fluids in strong-gravity spacetimes. Building on the existing relativistic hydrodynamics code Whisky, within the Einstein Toolkit framework, we introduce modifications to incorporate radiation fluids, including updates to the source terms, recovery scheme, and Riemann solvers. Modifications are validated using standard shock tube tests. We present results for radiation accretion onto a single black hole, as well as a photon star solution for radiation in unstable hydrostatic equilibrium, demonstrating both collapse and dispersion under perturbations.

cross.title: The Physics of Interstellar Travel
cross.summary: How can we send an uncrewed spacecraft to the nearest stars within a human lifetime? What propulsion methods are available? Will it survive impacts in the interstellar medium? What science will it do at its destination? How can it send back data over enormous distances? In this short semi-popular article, I examine various aspects of the physics of interstellar travel, its challenges and possible solutions. I focus on nuclear rockets, laser sails, dust impacts, and communication. These, as well as other issues such as navigation and onboard power, are explored in more detail in my book, The Physics of Interstellar Travel (2026).

cross.title: Black-hole ringdown at an exceptional point
cross.summary: Black holes ring in damped oscillations. At an exceptional point, photon-sphere and near-horizon modes merge, and their response can acquire a linear time factor. We compute its amplitude from constrained Einstein-Maxwell data for a rotating, charged black hole in de Sitter space. With seven competing modes fixed, the late-time curvature error is 0.00383$\%$ for the pair and 0.01401$\%$ for a refitted exponential. We suppress the linear term by tuning the initial disturbance at fixed geometry. Hence, near coalescence, changing only the initial disturbance can shift the frequency inferred from a short ringdown fit.

cross.title: Effect of Turbulence and Inhomogeneities on the Propagation of Kinetic Scale Waves
cross.summary: Context. Electromagnetic ion-scale waves are well known to occur in the solar wind. Eikonal (WKB) like effects may play an important role in the interplay between the propagation and local kinetic plasma dynamics of ion cyclotron waves. Aims. This Letter aims to explore the interplay of ICW propagation with turbulence and local kinetic plasmas using ray tracing equations for ICWs in a moving medium, in which turbulent gradients are present. Methods. Parker Solar Probe observations of ICWs in the solar wind are studied using ray equations in a moving medium. Gradients in the dispersion relation responsible for WKB evolution of ICW are constrained and compared with a Parker spiral model. Results. The empirical gradients, which contain turbulent motions, greatly enhance the efficiency of WKB effects. However, the typical refraction rates are significantly slower than expected quasilinear evolution of the observed wave populations, which suggests that local kinetic physics dominates over nonlinear expansion effects. Conclusions. Turbulence can effectively increase WKB effects due to gradients caused by nonlinear interactions. In the solar wind these gradients are not sufficient to substantially change an individual ion-scale ICW over its lifetime. Incorporating kinetic effects of expansion may help advance the understanding of generation and absorption of ICW and their role in heating in the solar wind.

cross.title: SWXAI: A Unified Multimodal Explainability Library for Space Weather Forecasting and Heliophysics
cross.summary: Space weather forecasting and heliophysics increasingly rely on machine learning models that process heterogeneous inputs such as multi-viewpoint multi-wavelength solar images and rasters, multivariate time series, spatial annotations, and tabular event-level data. However, explainability workflows remain fragmented across libraries, model interfaces, and output formats, limiting reuse and reproducibility. We present SWXAI, an open-source library that unifies explainable AI (XAI) workflows for image, time-series, and tabular data in space weather forecasting and heliophysics. SWXAI provides a common, extensible interface across commonly used vision, time-series, and tabular learning models, with validation, adaptation, and persistent explanation objects. It also includes domain-grounded examples, reproducible notebooks, tests, and documentation, enabling users to inspect outputs, swap models or explainers, and extend workflows to new heliophysics datasets. SWXAI reduces modality-specific engineering overhead and supports comparable, reusable explanations across heterogeneous scientific machine learning pipelines. A benchmark against direct backend implementations shows that SWXAI substantially reduces the code users write to produce an explanation, with no practical runtime cost.

cross.title: Relative Entropy Methods for Rotating Stars in the Compressible Euler-Riesz Equations
cross.summary: We establish finite-time relative entropy estimates for axisymmetric finite-energy entropy solutions of the three-dimensional attractive compressible Euler-Riesz equations near a prescribed compactly supported rotating star. The entropy solutions are assumed to have the same total mass as the steady state and to satisfy the prescribed angular momentum relation. For general pressure laws, the compatibility with the angular momentum constraint, together with the nonnegative rotational remainder, yields a cancellation of the centrifugal terms. For axisymmetric perturbations, the gradient of the perturbed Riesz potential has no azimuthal component and therefore couples only to those momentum components controlled by the modulated kinetic energy. The density-weighted estimates for the Riesz potential then allow us to close the relative entropy inequality. Under an additional higher-integrability assumption on the density, the result extends to the Chandrasekhar pressure law, yielding a corresponding stability estimate for rotating white dwarf stars.

cross.title: The first-order phase transitions and gravitational waves from an effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models
cross.summary: First-order phase transitions in the early Universe can generate stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds in frequency bands targeted by proposed deci-Hz observatories. We study the gravitational-wave consequences of the right-handed gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2)_{R_1}\times SU(2)_{R_2}\to SU(2)_R$ in a Pati-Salam effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models. The ultraviolet construction fixes the gauge structure and particle multiplicities, while the scalar masses and quartic couplings are treated as renormalized inputs below the supersymmetry-breaking scale. Using a one-loop finite-temperature potential with ring resummation, we follow a strongly supercooled transition at the few-TeV scale through nucleation, percolation, completion, and reheating. The leading-order friction diagnostic does not support a runaway wall, so sound waves dominate the gravitational-wave signal, with turbulence as a sub-leading contribution; the finite acoustic lifetime suppresses the peak. For the fast-wall reference case, the spectrum peaks at $f_{\rm peak}=0.611$ Hz with $h^2\Omega_{\rm GW,peak}=1.232\times10^{-11}$, in the deci-Hz band targeted by DECIGO and BBO. We present its dependence on the wall speed, renormalization scale, and thermal screening, together with a noise-only comparison for several proposed detector configurations.

cross.title: Probing Exotic Electron-Electron Interactions via Adiabatic Spin Inversion in MRFM
cross.summary: Light bosons beyond the Standard Model can mediate exotic spin-dependent interactions between electrons, motivating sensitive searches at short distances. We propose a magnetic resonance force microscopy (MRFM) scheme that exploits oscillating-cantilever-driven adiabatic reversals (OSCAR) of electron spins to convert these interactions into measurable mechanical signals. The ferromagnetic tip serves as both a dense polarized-spin source and a source of magnetic-field gradients, enabling force detection without magnetic shielding between the source and sensor. Within a linearized treatment of the coupled spin-mechanical dynamics, we derive resonance-frequency shifts associated with the $V_2$ and $V_3$ interactions and a second-harmonic force signal arising from the velocity-dependent $V_8$ interaction. We further investigate interrupted-OSCAR differential detection and distance-dependent measurements to discriminate exotic signals from conventional magnetic backgrounds. Using representative parameters from ensemble and single-spin MRFM experiments, we estimate the projected sensitivity under specified noise and statistical assumptions. The results suggest that the proposed scheme could provide complementary sensitivity to short-range spin-dependent interactions, with the potential to improve existing constraints on $V_2$ over selected submicrometer interaction ranges. Our study establishes adiabatic spin-inversion MRFM as a promising approach to probing exotic electron-electron forces.

cross.title: Pushing the accuracy of the quasi-circular baseline for the SEOBNR family of models
cross.summary: Gravitational-wave observations have opened a new era of astronomy, with accurate modeling of binary black hole signals becoming increasingly important for source characterization and astrophysical inference as detector sensitivities improve. We present SEOBNRv5iHM, an updated quasi-circular, aligned-spin inspiral-merger-ringdown gravitational-waveform model with higher-order modes, constructed within the effective-one-body formalism and building upon SEOBNRv5HM. The improvements mainly concern the late inspiral and the merger-ringdown: we remove the non-quasi-circular corrections used in previous models and instead introduce a phenomenological intermediate region between the inspiral and the ringdown, which allows the ringdown attachment time to be chosen independently for each mode, including at the peak of the mode's amplitude. The model is calibrated and validated against 591 quasi-circular aligned-spin waveforms from the third Simulating eXtreme Spacetimes catalog. For the $(2,2)$ mode, when considering the maximum unfaithfulness against numerical relativity over a total mass range of 10-300$M_\odot$, SEOBNRv5iHM achieves a median of $4.25\times10^{-5}$, a factor of 4.5 below SEOBNRv5HM, and a factor of 3-8 below other semi-analytical models, with $84\%$ of cases below $10^{-4}$. For $M\ge150 M_\odot$, the median drops to $9.7\times10^{-6}$, comparable to the numerical-relativity surrogate NRHybSur3dq8. For polarization mismatches at inclination $\pi/3$, with modes up to $\ell_\mathrm{max} = 5$, the median maximum unfaithfulness is $4.2\times10^{-4}$, a factor of 2.6 below SEOBNRv5HM, 1.9 below IMRPhenomTHM, and 6-11 below the other semi-analytical models. Since spin-precessing and eccentric models are built on top of the quasi-circular, aligned-spin baseline, these improvements will make future SEOBNR models more accurate, reducing waveform systematics in upcoming analyses.

cross.title: Horizon-penetrating rotating black-hole configurations in VCDM
cross.summary: A regular black-hole metric need not define a regular configuration of VCDM, whose preferred foliation is part of the gravitational solution. We construct stationary rotating, possibly charged configurations on the constant-auxiliary Einstein-Maxwell branch. Their Kerr-Newman and Kerr-Newman-de Sitter geometries carry nonzero constant-mean-curvature foliations that cross the future black-hole horizon and, in the de Sitter case, the future cosmological horizon. A horizon-regular flux formulation specifies the inner data and the distinct hyperboloidal and expanding asymptotic ends. Seventeen survey configurations are supplemented by a mean-flux scan at fixed four-geometry and paired flat/de Sitter comparisons down to $\kappa M = 0.01$, where $K_0 = 3\kappa$. Varying the flux changes the preferred-foliation shear without changing the background seen by standard test matter. The paired local lapse and shear differences have effective powers close to two over the computed range, with the lapse comparison requiring a fixed time normalization. Continuous residuals, geometric reconstructions, and selected grid comparisons test the numerical solutions. An exact lapse bound excludes zeros in the regular stationary exterior block with $\Delta_r > 0$. We distinguish singular finite-proper-distance endpoints from asymptotic trumpet ends and give conditional bounds on a stationary spacelike inner limit. A local cosmological interpretation requires additional matching assumptions; dynamical selection and the rotating interior endpoint are not determined by the stationary construction.

cross.title: Quasinormal Modes of Black holes in the generalized Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution of $f(R)$ gravity
cross.summary: We analyze scalar, vector, and {axial} tensor perturbations in a Schwarzschild-type static spherically symmetric solution of modified $f(R)$ gravity. This solution differs from the Schwarzschild metric of general relativity through the presence of a linearly growing term and a logarithmic correction, and it depends on four integration constants. Using the higher-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation and an analytical method, we calculate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) for all three types of perturbations. Our results show that, for appropriately chosen parameter values, the QNMs closely match those of the Schwarzschild black hole. In particular, the model parameter $A$ produces a nonlinear increase in both the oscillation frequency and damping rate of ringdown gravitational waves. A similar effect arises for the parameter $\eta$ when $A$ is small, while for larger $A$ values the effects are opposite, where the scalar perturbations display a distinct deviation compared to the vector and {axial} tensor cases. Contour plots of QNMs in the parameter space support these findings. Finally, time-domain profiles are obtained to illustrate the dynamical evolution of the gravitational wave signal.

cross.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Bayesian Inference for Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
cross.summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) pose a major challenge to Bayesian parameter inference because of their complex, highly multimodal likelihood surfaces. Locating narrow high-likelihood regions is particularly difficult without knowledge of the true source parameters, which is unavailable in real observations. We develop a deep-learning-assisted Bayesian inference framework that combines neural-network-guided parameter-space localization, particle swarm optimization, and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. Applied to simulated six-month EMRI signals, the framework recovers posterior distributions in close agreement with reference MCMC analyses initialized near the true parameter values, without requiring such knowledge for initialization. Once the neural network has been trained, the complete inference pipeline takes approximately 10 hours per signal.

cross.title: A Poisson-bracket operator for Hamiltonian separability: intrinsic geometry and exact defects
cross.summary: Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional. For Hamiltonians with a cyclic angle, the linearised operator divided by the squared rotor frequency is an angle derivative of the Melnikov integrand, so that the defect integrated along a homoclinic orbit decides the first-order splitting of the separatrix. Closed-form defects are obtained for the polar-nodal normal forms of satellite theory and, through a covariance of the operator on level sets, for Kerr geodesics. Used for coordinate selection, the defect singles out the separating focal distance of the Euler two-centre problem as its unique nondegenerate minimum, and for axisymmetric potentials it shows that the prescriptions of Sanders and Vasiliev are two weightings of the same Stäckel residual. The residual selector and Binney's shell-orbit fit improve both actions over the median prescription for 48 and 50 of 50 orbits in a flattened logarithmic potential, whereas the operator selector lowers the 90th-percentile action spread of 50 orbits in a Miyamoto-Nagai potential from 2.90% to 0.91%.

cross.title: SuperWIMPs in the Kination Era: Imprints on $N_{\rm eff}$ and CMB Spectral Distortions
cross.summary: We investigate how the late-time decays of unstable particles into dark matter and neutrinos can leave measurable imprints on both cosmological observables and collider experiments. We study this mechanism within the scotogenic model, where the lightest singlet fermion $N_1$ serves as the dark matter candidate and is produced via the late decay of the lightest inert doublet scalar via the superWIMP mechanism. By incorporating a kination-dominated era in the early Universe, the altered expansion rate allows to match the observed $N_1$ relic density in parameter regions that would be underabundant in standard cosmology. The energy exchange between the injected neutrinos and photons resulting from the late-time decay can produce CMB spectral $\mu$-distortions, detectable shifts in the effective number of relativistic species $N_{\rm eff}$, or both simultaneously. Concentrating on the lightest component of inert doublet scalars with masses between $200$ and $500~\text{GeV}$, we find that these cosmological signals are accompanied by complementary signatures accessible at the LHC. Although our analysis is derived within the scotogenic framework, our findings apply more broadly to scenarios in which the unstable particle undergoes late-time out-of-equilibrium decay to produce dark matter and non-thermal neutrinos, offering how future CMB measurements and collider searches can jointly probe dark matter production and the early Universe's thermal history.

cross.title: A Self-Interacting Dark-Matter Route to Supermassive Kerr Black Holes via Super-Eddington Bondi Accretion: Mass-Spin Evolution
cross.summary: Recent JWST observations motivate mechanisms for rapid black-hole growth in the early Universe. Extending our previous Schwarzschild study, we show that critical relativistic Bondi accretion of repulsively self-interacting dark matter remains an efficient super-Eddington channel for Kerr black holes with rotating inflow. Within a stationary equatorial quasi-spherical framework, smooth critical solutions exist over a finite range of inflow angular momentum set by the Kerr marginally bound capture values. Rotation changes the sonic structure and accretion efficiency, while the critical density cancellation and dark-sector/halo matching retain their Schwarzschild form. The resulting rapid growth persists until the finite halo supply becomes limiting. Because the inflow also carries angular momentum, stellar-mass seeds can grow and spin up simultaneously; illustrative population evolutions therefore provide a joint mass--spin route to early supermassive Kerr black holes.

cross.title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
cross.summary: Reabsorption of Urca neutrinos suppresses the bulk-viscous damping predicted for neutron star merger oscillations. Below the direct-Urca threshold the capture neutrinos have mean energies of 19-46 MeV and are absorbed within metres. An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives 2.7 s for a 1-kHz, 10-km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. It holds across the sampled states, three equations of state and the rate variations, with nearly frozen composition. This absorption is present in full-kinematics rates and absent from elastic opacity tables.

cross.title: Naturalness in the Past from a Time-Dependent Supersymmetry Scale
cross.summary: We consider the possibility that electroweak naturalness may be epoch dependent. In no-scale supergravity, a rolling quintessence modulus can control the supersymmetry-breaking scale, allowing superpartners to be much lighter in the early universe while remaining heavy today. Fifth-force and varying-constant effects can be suppressed via correlated modular weights in the visible-sector Kähler metric and modulus-dependent superpotential Yukawa couplings, while radiative stability of the quintessence potential requires additional tuning of the field-dependent vacuum energy. The resulting effective theory has distinctive implications for early-universe phase transitions, relic abundances, and gravitational waves.

cross.title: Quality time in extra dimensions: axion quality and radion cosmology
cross.summary: Higher-form symmetries can protect extra-dimensional axions, but additional symmetry breaking can still spoil the solution to the strong CP problem. We focus on electrically charged matter and magnetic gauging in a five-dimensional circle compactification where the axion arises from an Abelian gauge field and the radius is dynamical. We discuss two mechanisms for stabilising the radius/radion using Casimir energy from fields neutral under the Abelian gauge field, with and without an additional periodic scalar winding around the compact circle. Both admit Minkowski and de Sitter minima. At the Minkowski minima (with radion masses of $100$--$170\,\mathrm{TeV}$), electrically charged matter induces a residual strong CP angle of order $10^{-17}$ and shifts the radius negligibly. Magnetic gauging remains compatible after including its additional degree of freedom in the Casimir spectrum, provided its coupling is sufficiently small. We observe that increasing the radius suppresses charged-matter breaking relative to QCD but increases magnetic breaking contribution. We also determine the radion decay channels, including the graviphoton, and study reheating from a possible radion-dominated era without scalar winding or magnetic gauging. For a non-minimal Higgs-curvature coupling $\xi=7$, the visible-sector reheating temperature is about $85\,\mathrm{MeV}$ with a dark-radiation contribution of $\Delta N_{\rm eff}\approx0.02$. The entropy released during radion decay dilutes the axion abundance, allowing axions with $f_a=10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and an initial misalignment angle $\vartheta_i\approx0.43$ to account for the entire observed dark matter abundance. For the same decay constant, reproducing this abundance in radiation domination requires $\vartheta_i\approx0.065$.

cross.title: First demonstration of long-distance electron drift in liquid xenon with the Xenoscope time projection chamber
cross.summary: Xenoscope is a dual-phase xenon time projection chamber operated at the University of Zurich to investigate electron transport over distances relevant to the next-generation XLZD (XENON-LUX-ZEPLIN-DARWIN) observatory. We demonstrate electron drift over $2.6$ m in liquid xenon using cosmic-muon-induced ionization signals. External muon tagging provides a timing reference for charge produced at known depths, while the endpoint of the average electroluminescence waveform probes transport over the full drift length. We measure electron drift velocities of $(1.320 \pm 0.006)$ mm/$\mu$s at $(80.92 \pm 0.36)$ V/cm and $(1.436 \pm 0.001)$ mm/$\mu$s at $(96.00 \pm 0.42)$ V/cm. These results establish detectable charge transport over meter-scale distances and provide an experimental benchmark for the development of future large liquid-xenon time projection chambers.

cross.title: Numerical-Relativity Particle-in-Cell Simulations: Self-Gravitating Collisionless Matter in Dynamical Spacetimes
cross.summary: Gravitational collapse and instability, black-hole dynamics in systems with large scale separations, and questions surrounding extremal black hole formation require full nonlinear studies using accurate and adapted numerical tools. To this end, we present a new algorithm to study collisionless relativistic systems using a fully kinetic description of matter coupled to the evolving spacetime. In detail, we present a numerical-relativity particle-in-cell (NRPIC) framework for solving the Einstein--Vlasov system in three spatial dimensions. Implemented on top of the performance-portable \texttt{AthenaK} code, the method couples particle dynamics to Z4c spacetime evolution in moving puncture gauge through conservative stress-energy deposition on adaptively refined meshes. Our implementation makes use of advances in the computational modeling of relativistic plasmas using modern PIC models, now made available to general-relativistic gravity via an equivalent electrodynamic formulation. We introduce a Boris-type particle pusher that exploits the electrodynamic (Lorentz force) form of the geodesic force. We validate the coupled evolution against spherical dust collapse, follow prolate collapse through collisionless caustics into black-hole formation, and investigate the stability and nonlinear migration of relativistic clusters. Highlighting its potential to study gravitational instability in NR, we simulate the collapse of two overdensities within a common collisionless envelope, following black-hole formation, binary inspiral and merger, and subsequent mass accretion onto the remnant.

repl.title: Global MHD simulations of the solar convective zone using a volleyball mesh decomposition. I. Pilot
repl.summary: Solar modelling has long been split into `internal' and `surface' modelling because of the lack of tools to connect the very different scales in space and time, as well as the widely different environments and the dominating physical effects involved. Significant efforts have recently been put into resolving this disconnect. We address the outstanding bottlenecks in connecting internal convection zone and dynamo simulations to the surface of the Sun, and conduct a proof-of-concept high-resolution global simulation of the convection zone of the Sun, using the task-based DISPATCH code framework. We present a new `volleyball' mesh decomposition, which has Cartesian patches tessellated on a sphere with no singularities. We use our new entropy based HLLS approximate Riemann solver to model magneto-hydrodynamics in a global simulation, ranging between 0.655---0.998 R$_\odot$, with an initial ambient magnetic field set to 0.1 Gauss. This paper describes the methods and the pilot runs of the setup. The mesh decomposition exhibits neither unwanted artefacts, nor noise build-up. The simulations develop convective motions with complex, turbulent structures. Small-scale dynamo action twists the ambient magnetic field and locally amplifies magnetic field magnitudes by more than two orders of magnitude within the initial run-time.

repl.title: Measuring the Hubble Constant Using Strongly Lensed Gravitational Wave Signals
repl.summary: The measurement of the Hubble constant $H_0$ plays an important role in the study of cosmology. In this letter, we propose a new method to constrain the Hubble constant using the strongly lensed gravitational wave (GW) signals. By reparameterizing the waveform, we find that the lensed waveform is sensitive to the $H_0$. Assuming the scenario that no electromagnetic counterpart of the GW source can be identified, our method can still give meaningful constraints on the $H_0$ with the information of the lens redshift. We then apply Fisher information matrix and Markov Chain Monte Carlo to evaluate the potential of this method. For the space-based GW detector, TianQin, the $H_0$ can be constrained within a relative error of $\sim$ 0.3-2\%, using a single strongly lensed GW event. Precision varies according to different levels of electromagnetic information.

repl.title: Exploring tidal dissipation in rubble pile binary secondaries using a discrete element model
repl.summary: In this work, models of rubble pile binary secondaries are simulated in various spin states in a system similar in size and scale to Didymos-Dimorphos. The numerical modeling is performed in the N-body Chrono-based software GRAINS, which simulates gravity, contact, and friction forces acting on non-spherical mass elements. In a high-fidelity, high-performance computational setting, tidal dissipation successfully emerges in the simulations as a consequence of the effects of inter-element contact and friction across thousands of simulated nonspherical mass elements. We devise computational techniques and rigorous numerical procedures for studying tides in the well-established framework of GRAINS. The simulations reveal tidal deformation, phase lag, and secular spin-down, including the transition from super-synchronous rotation to synchronous libration. We also observe the exchange of energy and angular momentum between the secondary's rotation and orbit, and identify the semidiurnal tidal response through spectral and topographical analyses. Using both energy and torque-based calculations, we compute values of $Q/k_{2} \sim O(10^{2})$, whereas this value has been predicted by other studies to lie in the range $10^{2}<Q/k_{2}<10^{6}$. Further study is required to determine whether this result is representative of truly enhanced dissipativity, or a consequence of material or modeling assumptions. More broadly, this framework provides a numerical laboratory for investigating the granular mechanisms underlying tidal dissipation and their relationship to the macroscopic tidal response of rubble-pile bodies.

repl.title: EGS-z11-R0: a red, dust-rich galaxy at Cosmic Dawn
repl.summary: Context. Galaxies discovered by JWST at z > 10 are predominantly characterized by extremely blue rest-frame UV slopes. Conversely, the existence of dust-reddened systems at such early epochs has remained largely unconfirmed spectroscopically. Aims. We present the spectroscopic confirmation of EGS-z11-R0 at z = 11.45, the most distant red galaxy identified to date, discovered serendipitously through inspection of publicly available JWST/NIRSpec data. Methods. We analyze JWST/NIRSpec PRISM and G395M spectroscopy together with multiwavelength HST, NIRCam, and MIRI photometry. We identify significant detections of the C IV 1548,1551 and C III] 1908 transitions, yielding a redshift of zspec = 11.452 +/- 0.021. We measure rest-frame UV emission-line fluxes and equivalent widths and use these diagnostics to constrain the nature of the ionizing radiation field. Finally, we perform spectral energy distribution modeling with CIGALE, combining spectroscopy with photometry and including stellar, nebular, dust, and active galactic nuclei (AGN) components. Results. EGS-z11-R0 exhibits a red UV continuum slope (betaUV approximately -1.0), placing it well above the canonical MUV-betaUV relation at z~10-12 and making it the highest-z spectroscopically confirmed member of the emerging "red monster" population. Emission-line diagnostics reveal a hard ionizing spectrum consistent with extreme star formation and compatible with a composite stellar plus AGN scenario. The best-fit SED solution favors a stellar mass of log(M*/Msun) ~ 9.2-9.6, a SFR of 10-40 Msun yr^-1, and substantial dust attenuation (AV~1.2 mag). Conclusions. The confirmation of EGS-z11-R0 establishes that chemically evolved, dust-enriched galaxies were already in place at z approximately 11.5. [abridged]

repl.title: Learning What's Real: Disentangling Signal and Measurement Artifacts in Multi-Sensor Data, with Applications to Astrophysics
repl.summary: Data collected from the physical world is always a combination of multiple sources: an underlying signal from the physical process of interest and a signal from measurement-dependent artifacts from the sensor or instrument. This secondary signal acts as a confounding factor, limiting our ability to extract information about the physics underlying the phenomena we observe. Furthermore, it complicates the combination of observations in heterogeneous or multi-instrument settings. We propose a deep learning framework that leverages overlapping observations, a dual-encoder architecture, and a counterfactual generation objective to disentangle these factors of variation. The resulting representations explicitly separate intrinsic signals from sensor-specific distortions and noise, and can be used for counterfactual view generation, parameter inference unconfounded by measurement distortions, and instrument-independent similarity search. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on astrophysical galaxy images from the DESI Legacy Imaging Survey (Legacy) and the Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) Survey as a representative multi-instrument setting. This framework provides a general recipe for scientific and multi-modal self-supervised pretraining: construct training pairs from overlapping observations of the same physical system, treat sensor- or modality-specific effects as augmentations, and learn invariant representations through counterfactual generation.

figures.caption: Counterfactual Reconstruction. The model learns to disentangle intrinsic galaxy properties from instrument systematics by reconstructing an anchor image. Training uses data triplets : an anchor observation (signal source s s from instrument i i ), an instrument-augmented observation ( same source s s , a different instrument i ′ i^{\prime} ), and a physics-augmented observation (a different source s ′ s^{\prime} , same instrument i i ). The physics encoder extracts latents from the instrument-augmented pair to capture invariant physical features, while the instrument encoder processes the physics-augmented observation to capture instrument-specific effects . These latent variables jointly condition the flow-matching decoder. Crucially, the anchor image is never fed into the encoders; it is used only as a target for the flow-matching loss, forcing the model to generate the reconstruction counterfactually.

repl.title: Model-independent Constraints on Dark Energy Density from CMB-SPA, DESI DR2 BAO, and Updated Type Ia Supernova Compilations
repl.summary: Recent combinations of DESI BAO, CMB, and Type~Ia supernova data report a preference for evolving dark energy that is obtained within the $(w_0, w_a)$ parameterization and depends on the choice of SN~Ia compilation. We constrain the dark energy density ratio $X(z) \equiv \rho_{\rm DE}(z)/\rho_{\rm DE}(0)$ at five redshifts over $0 < z < 2.33$, without assuming a parametric form for the equation of state, using CMB data from SPT-3G, Planck~2018, and ACT~DR6 (hereafter CMB-SPA), DESI~DR2 BAO, and the updated Pantheon+, Union3.1, and DES-Dovekie SN~Ia compilations. For all three compilations, $X(z)$ rises above unity at low redshift, crosses unity near $z \approx 1$, and falls below unity at higher redshift. Depending on the SN~Ia compilation, the preference for a departure from a cosmological constant is $2.3$--$2.8\sigma$ with the five $X(z)$ knots, compared with $3.0$--$3.2\sigma$ in the $(w_0, w_a)$ parameterization. Because $X(z)$ is constrained locally in redshift, we can trace how the $\Lambda$CDM tension between each pair of probes propagates into its shape. The tension between BAO and the CMB in the $h r_d$--$\Omega_m$ plane reproduces this "see-saw" shape, whereas the $\Omega_m$ tension between SNe~Ia and the CMB only raises $X(z)$ slightly and nearly uniformly. The origin of the BAO--CMB tension can be tested by Euclid and Roman BAO measurements at $z \gtrsim 1$. We derive the distance prior $(R, \ell_A, \omega_b)$ from CMB-SPA data and show that it retains essentially all the information on $X(z)$ in the CMB-SPA power spectra without the lensing reconstruction, and that adding the lensing reconstruction only marginally increases the information on dark energy. Our work demonstrates the importance of model independence in exploring the nature of dark energy.

repl.title: Magnetic properties of the Abell 3391-3395 system revealed using wide-field MeerKAT polarimetry
repl.summary: Magnetic fields in cluster outskirts and the intercluster medium are poorly constrained because diffuse synchrotron emission is hard to detect at low surface brightness. Faraday rotation measures (RMs) of polarized background sources can probe foreground large-scale structure. The nearby interacting Abell 3391-3395 system hosts a well-established X-ray bridge, making it an excellent target for studying magnetization in the intercluster environment. We characterize the magnetized environment of Abell 3391/95 and its surroundings by constructing a dense RM grid from wide-field polarimetry. We observed Abell 3391/95 with MeerKAT in full polarization using a three-pointing mosaic. The data were calibrated with direction-independent and direction-dependent techniques and imaged using visibility-plane mosaicing for a large field of view at high sensitivity. Using Faraday synthesis, we formed Faraday cubes and measured RMs for polarized background sources. We defined on- and off-target regions using contours from a wavelet-filtered eROSITA image. We identified 434 polarized sources within the field, with a polarized source density ranging from about 30 sources per square degree in the outer regions to about 110 sources per square degree in the central field, and a field-averaged density of 73 sources per square degree. The clusters show a statistically significant enhancement of RM scatter relative to the off-target region. In contrast, the bridge shows comparatively low RM scatter, while an RM structure-function analysis on matched angular scales yields a tentative indication of larger RM differences in the bridge than off-target. Combined with low per-source depolarization, this suggests a bridge magnetic field relatively ordered on ~10 kpc scales, but less ordered on larger scales. The non-detection of diffuse synchrotron emission in the bridge yields improved upper limits on the emissivity.

repl.title: The Hunt for Red Dual AGNs I: Spatially-Resolved Mid-IR Dual AGNs in the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys
repl.summary: Theoretical studies predict that dual AGNs are a critical stage of galaxy merger-driven supermassive black hole growth. Systematic searches for dual AGNs typically target late-stage mergers ($\leq10$ kpc nuclear separations) and select AGNs based on optical diagnostics. Yet, simulations predict that obscuration can occur early in the merger sequence, and that a significant fraction of dual AGNs can be found beyond $10$ kpc. Here, we report on a new sample of 155 spatially resolved mid-IR dual AGNs candidates selected based upon their mid-IR $W1-W2$ colors from the Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer and optically classified as galaxy merger candidates using imaging from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Preliminary spectroscopic results are presented for approximately 2/3 of the sample. 78 candidates have been confirmed to reside in galaxy mergers; among these, 13 have been confirmed as bona fide mid-IR dual AGNs, while 65 represent strong dual AGN candidates that require further examination. 48 candidates have been rejected as non-merger contaminants (foreground-background AGNs, separations inconsistent with interacting galaxies, etc.). 29 candidates still await spectroscopic coverage. The confirmed and high confidence dual AGN candidates exhibit separations of 14.5-129 kpc; $>50%$ reside at separations $>50$ kpc. Confirmed and high confidence candidates also exhibit a diversity of nuclear optical BPT classes. Seyfert-Seyferts and Seyfert-HIIs dominate the overall BPT pairings. 31% of confirmed mid-IR dual AGNs reside in multi-mergers involving three or more galaxies. The diversity in AGN properties and environments identified in this work highlights the importance of multiwavelength selection strategies and analyses in the quest to holistically understand dual AGNs as a population.

repl.title: Eccentric Stellar-mass Binary Black Holes: Population, Detectability, and Waveform Analysis in the LISA and LIGO Era
repl.summary: Eccentric binary black holes (BBHs) formed through dynamical interactions can significantly contribute to gravitational wave (GW) detections. In this work, we present a simulated catalog of dynamically-formed, stellar-mass BBHs in the local universe, incorporating contributions from the Galactic field (flyby interactions), Galactic nucleus (eccentric Kozai-Lidov evolution), and globular clusters (N-body interactions). Our results predict a wide, highly eccentric BBH population in the Milky Way (MW), with source counts of $\sim 25, 9, 3, 1, <1$ for a 4-year LISA mission and $\sim 36, 13, 5, 2, 1$ for a 10-year mission, at $\mathrm{SNR} > 1, 3, 8, 20, 50$, respectively. Extending this model to cosmological populations, we show that different dynamical channels can produce distinct eccentricity distributions in the LVK band and can contribute hundreds of additional low-SNR mHz sources. Specifically, our model yields a merger rate of $\Gamma \sim 9 \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and $\sim 150$ extragalactic mHz BBHs with $\mathrm{SNR} > 1$. However, due to the lower mass and weaker GW signals of stellar-mass BBHs, this number declines sharply at higher detection thresholds (e.g., $\sim 1$ for $\mathrm{SNR} > 8$). We further highlight the impact of eccentric BBH signals on the LISA global fit, showing that their individual harmonics can be independently detected in the Milky Way, and may mimic circular binaries with systematically biased chirp masses. Lastly, we show that post-Newtonian waveforms converge reliably for eccentric BBHs with masses of $\lesssim 10^3 M_\odot$ in the mHz band. Overall, eccentric BBHs represent a prevalent and promising target for future space-based GW observatories. The simulated catalog and the LISA Eccentricity Astrophysics Package (LEAP) developed in this work are publicly available at this https URL .

repl.title: Spectro Capture: A Software System for Automated Small-Observatory Spectroscopy
repl.summary: Spectro Capture is a Python-based software system developed to automate small- observatory fibre-fed spectroscopy. The system integrates target selection, telescope slewing, guide star acquisition, fibre position restoration, calibration and science exposure sequencing within a single observing workflow. The paper describes the design and operational behaviour of the system at Shenton Park Observatory, where it has been used for unattended multi-target spectroscopic observing. Log analysis from January to May 2026 shows that the system completed 339 of 345 attempted science target blocks in primary unattended batch runs, corresponding to a completion rate of 98.3%. The results demonstrate that reliable unattended spectroscopy is practical at a small observatory when target acquisition, guiding, scheduling and calibration control are treated as an integrated software problem.

repl.title: Loss-Cone-Limited Dark Matter Capture by Early Black Hole Seeds
repl.summary: The rapid appearance of supermassive black holes at high redshift motivates a reassessment of non-baryonic growth channels. We develop a new loss-cone framework for collisionless dark-matter (DM) capture by early black-hole seeds, with particular attention to phase-space depletion and refilling. The calculation combines Eddington-inverted NFW-like halos, a relativistic direct-capture boundary, and an orbit-averaged Fokker-Planck treatment of angular-momentum transport. Primordial black holes (PBHs) are treated as massive perturbers whose refilling strength depends on both their abundance and individual mass. Collisionless refilling by triaxial or chaotic centrophilic orbits is included as a phenomenological upper-envelope channel. We show that ordinary stellar relaxation gives negligible DM-driven growth for the fiducial high-redshift seeds. PBH-driven granularity can yield order-of-magnitude growth in sufficiently compact halos, while triaxial or full-loss-cone supply can produce a rapid early burst. In the self-consistent calculations, however, the evolution generally becomes supply-limited. Once the accessible low-angular-momentum phase-space reservoir is depleted, the capture rate collapses and the black-hole mass saturates. Fixed-background NFW calculations therefore overestimate sustained growth, especially in the full-loss-cone limit. A TNG50-calibrated NFW benchmark gives negligible growth even under optimistic refilling assumptions. Collisionless DM capture is therefore unlikely to solve early SMBH growth in generic NFW-like halos, but it can provide a radiatively dark upper envelope in rare compact environments with efficient angular-momentum refilling.

repl.title: Neutron Star Mass-Radius Constraints for EXO 0748$-$676 from 2008-2025 Quiescent X-ray Spectra
repl.summary: We present new constraints on the mass and radius of the neutron star in the neutron star low-mass X-ray binary EXO 0748$-$676 obtained from a joint analysis of 20 quiescent X-ray observations obtained between 2008 and 2025, including 14 Chandra and 6 XMM-Newton exposures. These data sample two quiescent episodes separated by the 2024$-$2025 outburst. We model the 0.5$-$10 keV spectra with a hydrogen-atmosphere model, assuming a source distance of 7.1 kpc. In a global Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis in which the hydrogen column density, neutron star mass, and radius are tied across all observations, we obtain a neutron-star mass of $1.77^{+0.17}_{-0.22}\,M_\odot$ and a radius of $12.62^{+0.56}_{-0.74}$ km ($1\sigma$ credible intervals). We further perform independent fits to the first and second quiescent epochs and find that the combined data set significantly reduces the low-mass tail in the posterior distribution, leading to tighter lower bounds on the neutron-star mass. Incorporating the distance uncertainty of $7.1\pm1.2$ kpc, we conservatively constrain the neutron-star mass and radius to $M\simeq 1.41-2.11~M_{\odot}$ and $R\simeq 10.15-15.13$ km, favoring relatively stiff dense-matter equations of state. We also trace the thermal evolution across two quiescent epochs and find evidence for renewed crust cooling following the 2024$-$2025 outburst, providing a unique opportunity to compare the thermal relaxation behavior after two distinct accretion episodes.

repl.title: The kinetic-energy bottleneck in Fast Radio Burst models
repl.summary: Most Fast Radio Burst (FRB) models invoke a two-step process in which energy released by the central engine is converted into particle kinetic energy and subsequently radiated as coherent GHz emission. We derive model-independent constraints on this picture and apply them to the three main classes of FRB models. (i) Inner-magnetospheric models violate brightness-temperature and kinetic-luminosity limits unless particles are continuously re-accelerated in situ. Magnetar-strength fields can provide the required parallel electric field out to $R\lesssim10^{10}\mathrm{cm}$. Monster shocks provide continuous acceleration but, under a single-pass kinetic-energy interpretation, require extreme particle densities and predict emission well above GHz frequencies. Even mechanisms that bypass the kinetic bottleneck through conservative wave conversion remain subject to charge availability, which independently limits magnetospheric GHz production to $\lesssim 10^{10}$ cm for fiducial parameters. (ii) Light-cylinder forced-reconnection naturally provides continuous acceleration, but typically converts only $\lesssim10^{-6}$ of the injected energy into radio emission. (iii) External-shock maser models satisfy the kinetic-luminosity and brightness-temperature constraints, but the upstream wind is unavoidably optically thick to induced Compton scattering, independent of the model's principal parameters. Proposed escape routes - emission above the maser peak or upstream magnetization $\sigma_{\rm w}\gtrsim30$ imply very low efficiencies, while the former also conflicts with narrow FRB spectra. We conclude that near-surface magnetospheric models with continuous particle acceleration remain the most promising scenario, provided the radiation can escape the magnetosphere.

repl.title: Too shy to spin? Cosmic wallflowers as proto-globular clusters
repl.summary: We investigate the rotational properties of star-forming clusters at $z \sim 7.6$ in the high-resolution simulation MassiveBlackPS, focusing on two formation channels: clusters forming in galactic discs via gravitational instability and isolated circumgalactic systems, referred to as cosmic wallflowers, born out of cosmic filaments. Using stellar kinematics, we compare their rotational velocities, $v_{\rm rot}$, and rotational support, $v/\sigma$, to study whether formation environment leaves a clear dynamical imprint. We find a clear separation, wherein cosmic wallflowers systematically have lower rotational velocities and span a wide range in $v/\sigma$, whereas the identified disc clusters are strongly rotation-dominated and extend to higher $v_{\rm rot}$. When combined with stellar surface densities, a subset of the low-$v_{\rm rot}$ cosmic wallflowers lie surprisingly close to the observed globular cluster population in the Milky Way, whereas disc clusters remain offset. Within the cosmic wallflower population, we identify two regimes: lower-density, weakly rotating systems that overlap with these globular cluster properties, and denser, more rotationally supported systems that likely follow a different evolutionary pathway, possibly linking them to the origin of massive black hole seeds at high redshift. We further find that the gas content correlates with this behaviour, with gas-rich cosmic wallflowers preferentially occupying this low-rotation regime. This all suggests that environment and baryonic content together play a key role in setting the initial dynamical state and possible fate of clusters. In particular, weakly rotating, gas-rich cosmic wallflowers emerge as natural proto-globular cluster candidates, potentially evolving towards present-day systems through angular momentum loss and dynamical heating.

repl.title: The Maximum Initial Mass in low-thrust spacecraft trajectory design
repl.summary: We introduce the maximum-initial-mass problem as a standalone optimal-control formulation for low-thrust trajectory design and analyze its structure within Pontryagin's framework. For prescribed transfer time and endpoint states, the formulation maximizes the initial spacecraft mass, with necessary conditions yielding full-throttle control in the nondegenerate case and standard primer-vector steering. We establish that extremals of this single formulation correspond to extremals of two distinct problems: minimum-time and maximum-time transfer. The sign of the terminal dynamics-only Hamiltonian distinguishes the two normal representations, while the zero-Hamiltonian case admits an abnormal representation. We also clarify the relationship between free-time transversality and costate normalization in indirect formulations. This unified perspective offers two practical advantages. For reachability analysis, it replaces separate minimum- and maximum-time conditions with a single initial-mass threshold, simplifying both feasibility checks and the learning of reachability maps. For homotopy methods, it opens extended continuation paths that connect branches beyond those accessed by tracking individual time-optimal solutions. Applied to a benchmark multiple-revolution GTO-to-GEO transfer, the approach recovers the best known minimum-time solution, identifies previously unreported extremals, and reveals a funnel-like arrangement of transfer-time minima and maxima along a constant-initial-mass contour, including a previously reported trajectory that is a local maximum rather than a minimum.

repl.title: Neutron stars with an agnostic Dark sector: Core and Halo configurations from a two-fluid approach
repl.summary: The study of dark matter admixed neutron stars has the potential to advance our understanding of dark matter particle candidates. However, the large parameter space of dark matter particle masses restricts a systematic, model-independent study. In this analysis, we employ agnostic hadronic and dark-matter equations of state to construct dark-matter-admixed neutron stars within a two-fluid formalism. Dark matter is characterized solely by its low-density equation of state and mass and is modeled as a Fermi gas, while hadronic matter is anchored at low and high densities by chiral effective field theory and perturbative quantum chromodynamics calculations. A speed-of-sound parametrization describes the intermediate- and high-density regimes of both hadronic and dark matter, enabling an agnostic treatment of the dark matter equation of state that is constrained only by thermodynamic consistency and does not favor softer or stiffer behavior. Within this agnostic framework, we find that dark matter does not generically compactify the star: light dark matter forms extended halos that raise the tidal deformability, while heavy dark matter forms compact cores that lower it. Consequently, the dominant observational constraint shifts from gravitational-wave tidal deformability for light, halo-dominated models to NICER mass-radius data for heavy, core-dominated models. Using current data at $1\sigma$, we constrain the dark matter fraction to $f_{\mathrm{DM}} \lesssim 0.11$ for light dark matter. By treating the medium- and high-density dark matter equation of state agnostically within a fermionic framework, our approach yields conservative and broadly applicable bounds on the dark matter content of neutron stars. Neutron stars with similar masses but very different tidal deformabilities could be a smoking-gun signature of dark matter in neutron stars.

repl.title: Star Planet Interactions
repl.summary: Star-planet interactions (SPIs) describe the continuous exchange of energy, momentum, and mass between exoplanets and their host stars through radiative, tidal, magnetic, and particle-driven processes. Together, these interactions shape the structure, evolution, and observable properties of exoplanetary systems. In this review, we bring together current theoretical and observational understanding of SPIs, highlighting how stellar radiation, winds, and magnetic activity influence planetary atmospheres, interiors, and orbital evolution, while using the Solar System as a valuable reference for interpreting these processes. High-energy stellar radiation, particularly in the far- and extreme-ultraviolet and X-ray bands, drives atmospheric heating, photochemistry, ionisation, and escape. These effects are further influenced by stellar winds and magnetic interactions, which can either protect planetary atmospheres or accelerate their loss over time. Tidal interactions redistribute energy and angular momentum, producing internal heating and driving orbital migration and circularisation. Magnetic star-planet coupling provides additional pathways for energy transfer through reconnection and current systems, potentially enhancing atmospheric escape, heating planetary ionospheres and interiors, and generating observable signatures such as radio emission and enhanced stellar activity. We discuss how these processes work together, emphasising that their long-term impact depends on stellar evolution, planetary properties, atmospheric structure, and magnetic field strength. By presenting radiative, tidal, and magnetic interactions within a unified framework, this review highlights the physical mechanisms that shape planetary environments and identifies the key observational signatures that will complement future studies of exoplanet evolution and habitability.

repl.title: Fast and accurate bandpass integration of complex SEDs with neural networks
repl.summary: The paper presents a novel ML-based approach for fast and accurate bandpass integration of spectral energy distributions (SEDs). The non-locality of the integral operator involved guarantees the smoothness of the target function to be approximated, making it an excellent use-case for neural networks. The computational method developed for this work has been wrapped within pyfine (FINE: Fast Function Interpolation via NEural NEtworks). This new Python package makes the relevant code available and easy to use by everyone within the scientific community. The method is demonstrated with two different bandpass integration test cases with 3 and 9 free parameters, respectively, where both accuracy and computational performance are analyzed. The results show that the method is capable of predicting values of the bandpass integral with maximum relative residuals as low as 0.002% and 0.08% respectively, within the sampled region of the parameter space, fast run times, and very little memory overhead. The usage of pyfine is especially effective when the computation of an SED functional form, given a set of values for its free parameters, is expensive. However, already in the first of the two test cases, where a simple modified black body SED was employed, the neural network's measured run times resulted faster by two orders of magnitudes than an optimized multithreaded version of the ``brute force'' exact calculation of the integral.

repl.title: On Bimodality in the Eccentricity Distribution of Galactic Double Neutron Stars
repl.summary: The detection of Galactic double neutron stars (DNSs) through pulsar timing offers a unique opportunity to probe massive stellar and binary evolution. The current observed DNS population shows a scarcity of systems at intermediate eccentricities, although the present sample does not provide statistically significant evidence for an underlying bimodal distribution. We explore whether such a feature can arise naturally from DNS formation physics and serve as a prediction for future observations. We propose that this possible bimodality can result from a non-monotonic relationship between progenitor mass and neutron star (NS) mass, provided that the second-born NS receives a sufficiently small natal kick. We illustrate this scenario using the population synthesis code COMPAS, and find that our DNS population model produces an intermediate-eccentricity deficit broadly similar to that suggested by current observations and can reproduce the observed orbital period--eccentricity distribution relatively well. We also show that most measured second-born NS masses fall within the ranges predicted by our model at the corresponding DNS orbital eccentricities, providing a complementary observational diagnostic that is less sensitive to uncertainties in the preceding binary evolution. Our results therefore predict that an eccentricity bimodality should become more apparent as the Galactic DNS sample grows.

repl.title: Evidence for the Moon and Sun shadows with cosmic rays at an average energy of $\text{7}{\times}\text{10}^\text{17}\,$eV
repl.summary: Interactions of cosmic rays with the Moon and the Sun produce deficits in their arrival-direction distributions relative to an isotropic flux. Such shadows have been observed previously at energies between $10^{12}\,$eV and $10^{16}\,$eV. We report the first evidence for the Moon and Sun shadows at cosmic-ray energies larger than about $10^{16}\,$eV (average energy of $7\times10^{17}\,$eV), using data collected by the Pierre Auger Observatory. We employ data from three detector arrays covering $3000\,\text{km}^2$, $27\,\text{km}^2$, and $2\,\text{km}^2$, with spacings of $1500\,\text{m}$, $750\,\text{m}$, and $433\,\text{m}$, respectively. The data amount to over 10.6 million events. The Moon and Sun shadows are detected with a combined significance of approximately $3\sigma$. These observations confirm the pointing accuracy of the Surface Detector of the Pierre Auger Observatory using celestial bodies. From the combined Sun and Moon shadows, we infer an overall angular resolution of $(0.59^{+0.15}_{-0.11})^\circ$.

repl.title: The Galactic Neutrino Sky: Predictions from Gamma-ray Source Populations
repl.summary: High-energy neutrino emission from the Galactic plane has been detected at a significance of $5.7\sigma$, with a prominent excess toward the inner Galaxy. We show that this excess can be naturally explained by the spatial distribution of Galactic neutrino sources. By combining $\gamma$-ray source catalogs spanning GeV-PeV energies and selecting candidate hadronic emitters, we construct ReGal-$\gamma$, a template of resolved Galactic $\gamma$-ray sources that may also produce high-energy neutrinos. Compared with models of Galactic diffuse emission, ReGal-$\gamma$ predicts a neutrino intensity that is more strongly concentrated toward the inner Galaxy. Combined with models of diffuse cosmic-ray emission and unresolved $\gamma$-ray sources, the template reproduces both the spectral energy distribution and the Galactic longitudinal count profile reported by IceCube without requiring additional renormalization of the emission models. We test this result using an independent $\gamma$-ray source template constructed from different catalogs and find that our conclusion is robust against uncertainties in source modeling. Future measurements of the energy-dependent longitudinal and latitudinal neutrino distributions will provide tighter constraints on these models and help determine the spatial distribution of Galactic neutrino sources.

repl.title: A Sulfur-Rich Atmosphere for the Young Jupiter Analog AF Lep b Reveals Significant Solid Accretion
repl.summary: AF Lep b is one of the closest analogs to Jupiter in terms of mass ($3-4~M_{\rm{Jup}}$) and semi-major axis ($9$ AU) amenable to spectroscopic characterization. We present JWST/NIRSpec high-contrast spectroscopy of the planet from $2.85-5.3~\mu$m at $R\sim3000$, which provides detections of CO$_2$, H$_2$S, CH$_4$, $^{12}$CO (and $^{13}$CO), and H$_2$O, as well as complementary JWST/NIRCam imaging that captures the planet's continuum flux from $4.0-4.7~\mu$m. Combining the JWST observations with spectra from VLTI/GRAVITY and VLT/SPHERE ($1.0-2.5~\mu$m), we carry out atmospheric retrievals that include the effects of clouds and disequilibrium chemistry while allowing the C, O, and S abundances to vary independently. AF Lep b exhibits metal enrichment across C, O, and S with $\rm C/H=2.9\pm0.5$, $\rm O/H=3.7\pm0.6$, and $\rm S/H=4.7\pm0.7~\times$ solar (and stellar). The planet's slightly sub-solar C/O and C/S are consistent with formation near its observed location, and disfavor formation beyond the CO snowline. The sulfur enrichment in AF Lep b implies significant accretion of disk solids during formation, and we estimate the planet contains $56\pm7~M_{\oplus}$ of solids. The C, O, and S enrichment levels of AF Lep b are similar to those of Jupiter, and other super-Jupiters like HR 8799 bcde. We also show that the degree of atmospheric metal enrichment of these imaged planets is similar to the bulk metal enrichment of transiting gas giants with masses greater than $\sim1~M_{\rm{Jup}}$, suggesting that the process and efficiency of metal accretion for gas giants may not be strongly dependent on orbital distance or planet mass.

repl.title: A Radiation-Hydrodynamic Light Curve Grid and Interpolation Framework for Stripped-Envelope Supernovae
repl.summary: We present a grid of 7,560 stripped-envelope supernovae (SESNe) light curves based on radiation-hydrodynamic simulations of exploding helium-star progenitors. The grid spans an ejecta-mass range representative of typical SESNe, together with broad ranges of explosion energies, radioactive nickel masses, and degrees of material mixing. We systematically investigate how these physical parameters shape the light curves and develop an interpolation-based parameter inference framework that enables the application of the model grid to observational data. Using the simulated light curves as mock observations, we assess whether the input parameters can be recovered by the widely used Arnett model. Although it reproduces the overall light-curve morphology, the inferred ejecta masses show no significant correlation with the input values. Moreover, the analytical model produces a spurious correlation between the inferred explosion energy and nickel mass, despite these parameters being independent in the underlying model grid. These results demonstrate that neglecting physical processes naturally included in radiation-hydrodynamic models can lead to biased parameter inference, even when the overall light-curve morphology is well reproduced, and highlight the importance of physically motivated radiation-hydrodynamic models for the interpretation and the population study of SESNe.

repl.title: The low luminosity end of Galactic HMXBs with eROSITA: Establishing a luminosity floor for accreting BeXRBs
repl.summary: We present a first look at the Galactic population of heretofore known HMXBs as observed by SRG/eROSITA during its first four surveys. eROSITA's sensitivity of $\sim10^{-13}\,\mathrm{erg}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$, translating to $10^{32}$-$10^{34},\mathrm{erg}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ in luminosity for most known HMXBs in the Milky Way, has thus far never been reached by any wide-area survey instrument. We present the extended log N-log L distribution of known HMXBs reaching down to $10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ using eROSITA, and show the large scatter that can be induced by source intrinsic variability. We present sub-type resolved luminosity distributions, showing that the Supergiant X-ray binaries (SgXBs) and Be X-ray binaries (BeXRBs) occupy different parts of the overall distribution, and reanalyse RXTE/ASM data and MAXI for comparison to eROSITA. The luminosity regime uncovered by eROSITA allows a systematic study of the "transient" BeXRBs, which are typically below the detection threshold of monitors outside of outburst, and whose low luminosity behavior has been a longstanding question. Signatures of stable accretion at low luminosities have been observed with pointed instruments for a fraction of the overall sample, so far. With the eROSITA results, we posit that accretion outside of outburst is likely the norm, since a vast majority (> 80%) of BeXRBs are detected at luminosities at least an order of magnitude higher than expected for the most X-ray luminous Be stars. We discuss the observed luminosity in the context of cold disk accretion and the "propeller" mechanism. We highlight a small subpopulation of "isolated" Be-stars that reach luminosities comparable to the least luminous BeXRBs, hinting at the presence of compact object companions.

repl.title: Density-induced dark-baryon conversion in $Δ-$admixed hypernuclear neutron stars
repl.summary: We investigate density-induced conversion of neutrons into a neutral dark baryon $\chi$ in cold, charge-neutral, $\beta$-equilibrated neutron-star matter containing hyperons and all $\Delta(1232)$ quartet. The hadronic sector is modeled within a density-dependent covariant density-functional framework using the DDME2 parametrization. A scalar Higgs portal is included as a possible interaction channel between the visible and dark sectors, although its mean-field contribution is negligible for the couplings adopted here. Unlike fixed dark-matter admixture models or scenarios in which nucleon-to-DM conversion is driven by Higgs exchange, the $\chi$ abundance is determined self-consistently from chemical equilibrium and baryon-number conservation. We find that hyperons and $\Delta$ resonances alter the neutron chemical potential, delay the onset of $\chi$, and suppress its abundance relative to nucleonic matter. This competition induces characteristic changes in the equation of state, particle fractions, sound speed, and adiabatic index. For $m_\chi=1250$, $1300$, and $1400$ MeV, the maximum masses of the complete $N+Y+\Delta+\chi$ configurations are $1.806$, $1.899$ and $2.024,M_\odot$, respectively, indicating that the massive-pulsar constraint disfavors the lighter dark-baryon benchmarks. The radial profiles further show that for $m_\chi=1400$ MeV, $\chi$ is confined to the inner core of the most massive stars, while canonical configurations remain essentially unaffected. Thus, the stellar modifications arise primarily from conversion-induced rearrangement of the equilibrium composition rather than from Higgs-mediated interactions. These results highlight the importance of treating conventional non-nucleonic degrees of freedom and density-generated dark baryons on an equal footing when assessing the astrophysical viability of dark-sector extensions of dense matter.

repl.title: Particle acceleration in Alfvénic turbulence with a strong guide field
repl.summary: Magnetically dominated Alfvénic turbulence creates an effective environment for particle acceleration. However, when a strong mean field is present, traditional mechanisms like mirror and curvature acceleration become inefficient at explaining non-thermal particle energy distributions. Based on numerical and phenomenological study, we propose that in such turbulence, particles are accelerated in charge-starved current sheets, corresponding to current velocities approaching the speed of light. The distributions of the electric currents, plasma density, fluctuations of electric charge, as well as the energy distributions of accelerated particles, approximately follow log-normal statistics. Non-thermal particle distributions thus arise from particle acceleration in these charge-starved current sheets rather than from conventional Fermi-type particle acceleration by turbulent eddies.
